purpose: Source catalog and scope controls; not a clinical protocol, automatic prescription table, efficacy labels or expert-approved algorithm.

sources.title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
sources.scope: General public-health guidance for population groups; not individualized performance coaching
takeaways: Adults gain benefit from aerobic activity and muscle-strengthening work; begin gradually.
Guideline frequency/volume categories are population recommendations, not validated individual training-load ceilings.
prohibitedUses: Do not infer safety, readiness, or individual optimal mileage from weekly time alone.
Do not treat absence of source activity as inactivity.

sources.title: 2026 resistance training position stand update
sources.scope: Resistance exercise outcomes in healthy adults, with evidence review and goal-specific dose variables
takeaways: Consistency and gradual participation are central, including home and bodyweight exercise.
Resistance prescriptions may be goal-dependent, while some advanced techniques are optional.
prohibitedUses: Do not invent an athlete's tested 1RM or automatically require maximal loading.
Do not equate one generic rep target with a proven individual hypertrophy or strength response.

sources.title: How much is too much? Part 1: load in sport and risk of injury
sources.scope: Sport-load monitoring consensus; older evidence and population-specific limitations
takeaways: Individual training-load interpretation involves external training, internal response, and context.
No single marker reliably identifies all maladaptation or injury risks.
prohibitedUses: Do not hardcode a universal mileage increment or acute:chronic ratio as a proven injury-prevention threshold.
Do not diagnose overtraining or injury from isolated HRV/RHR/sleep values.

sources.title: How much is too much? Part 2: load in sport and risk of illness
sources.scope: Sport illness/load consensus; limited evidence for risk quantification across sports and populations
takeaways: Internal and external monitoring are complementary, with variability between athletes.
Life stress, travel and recovery are relevant context; evidence does not support universal illness thresholds.
prohibitedUses: Do not infer clinical illness from a synthetic readiness score.
Do not automatically add missed training volume after interruptions.

promoteToExecutableRuleOnlyAfter: source relevance to target user population reviewed
all assumption and measurement requirements documented
units and unsupported data cases specified
independent expert review where health/safety consequences require it
negative/edge-case and reproducible offline tests added
governance.rule: A URL or publication date is metadata, not evidence that a proposed coaching threshold is effective or safe for a particular athlete.
